query: Which event-study window lengths and lead/lag specifications best capture anticipation and delayed effects for shocks in a 6–9 month winery panel?

response.query: Which event-study window lengths and lead/lag specifications best capture anticipation and delayed effects for shocks in a 6–9 month winery panel?
response.answer: For a 6–9 month winery panel, a [-30,+30] event-study window captures anticipation and delayed effects. Lead/lag specifications should include pre- and post-shock periods.

results.title: Chapter 130A
results.content: (d) The list of essential public health services required by this section shall not be construed to limit or restrict the powers and duties of the Commission for Public Health or the Departments of Environmental Quality and Health and Human Services as otherwise conferred by State law. All records containing privileged patient medical information, information protected under 45 Code of Federal Regulations Parts 160 and 164, and information collected under the authority of Part 4 of Article 5 of this Chapter that are in the possession of the Department of Health and Human Services or local health departments shall be confidential and shall not be public records pursuant to G.S. 132-1. (a) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b1) of this section, and notwithstanding any other provision of Article 64 of Chapter 143 of the General Statutes to the contrary, a local government may adopt and enforce ordinances, board of health rules, and policies restricting or prohibiting smoking that are more restrictive than State law and that apply in local government buildings, on local government grounds, in local vehicles, or in public places.
